title: Motion graphs
examples: How do I find the speed from a v-t graph?
What does the area under the graph represent?
Can the slope of an s-t graph be negative?

explain.say: Today we will look at motion graphs. We will learn about s-t and v-t graphs. We will find the gradient and the area on these graphs.
The gradient of an s-t graph gives us the speed. Remember that the slope is rise over run. So, speed is the change in position divided by time.
If the gradient of an s-t graph is constant, the object moves at a steady speed. For example, if the graph goes up steadily, the speed is constant.
The area under a v-t graph gives us the distance traveled. This is a very useful thing to remember. We calculate the area using simple shapes.
To find the area, we can use rectangles or triangles. For example, a rectangle under the graph shows constant velocity over time.

faq.q: What does a zero gradient on an s-t graph mean?
faq.a: A zero gradient means the object is not changing its position. This tells us that the object is stationary or at rest.
asks: What does a flat line on the s-t graph mean?
If the gradient is zero, what is the speed?

faq.q: Does the area under a v-t graph always mean distance?
faq.a: Yes, for motion graphs, the area under the velocity-time graph represents the total distance covered. We must be careful with negative areas.
asks: How do I find distance from v-t?
Is area always distance in these graphs?

faq.q: What does the gradient of a v-t graph represent?
faq.a: The gradient of a velocity-time graph gives us the acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time.
asks: What is the slope of a v-t graph?
What does the gradient of v-t show?

faq.q: Can I find the distance if the graph is curved?
faq.a: If the graph is curved, you might need calculus to find the exact area. For simple shapes, like trapeziums, you can use standard area formulas.
asks: What if the graph is not a simple shape?
How do I find area for a curve?

faq.q: If the s-t graph has a negative gradient, what is happening?
faq.a: A negative gradient on an s-t graph means the object is moving back towards the starting point. This is negative displacement.
asks: What does a negative slope on s-t mean?

facts: The gradient of an s-t graph represents the instantaneous speed.
The area under a v-t graph represents the total displacement or distance.
A constant gradient on an s-t graph means constant speed.
The gradient of a v-t graph represents acceleration.

quiz.say: A graph shows position versus time. If the gradient is a constant positive value, what is the object doing?

options.show: Moving at a constant speed in one direction.
options.say: Moving at a constant speed in one direction.

quiz.why: The gradient on an s-t graph always gives the speed of the object.

wrong.1: Acceleration is related to the change in speed, not just the constant slope.
wrong.2: Resting objects have a zero gradient, not a constant positive one.
wrong.3: Slowing down means the gradient is decreasing, not constant.

quiz.say: A velocity-time graph forms a rectangle from time zero to ten seconds. What distance did the object cover?

options.show: The distance is the gradient of the graph.
options.say: The distance is the gradient of the graph.

options.show: The distance is the area of the rectangle, which is velocity multiplied by time.
options.say: The distance is the area of the rectangle, which is velocity multiplied by time.

options.show: The distance is ten times the velocity.
options.say: The distance is ten times the velocity.

options.show: The distance is zero because the graph is straight.
options.say: The distance is zero because the graph is straight.

quiz.why: The area under the v-t graph always calculates the total distance traveled.

wrong.0: The gradient of v-t is acceleration, not distance.
wrong.2: This confuses the formula and ignores the area concept entirely.
wrong.3: A straight line does not mean zero distance if the velocity is not zero.

quiz.say: If an object starts from rest and accelerates uniformly, what shape will the area under its v-t graph form over time?

options.show: The area will be a single point.
options.say: The area will be a single point.

options.show: The area will be zero because it is accelerating.
options.say: The area will be zero because it is accelerating.

options.show: The area will form a trapezium or a triangle, depending on the time.
options.say: The area will form a trapezium or a triangle, depending on the time.

options.show: The area will be a perfect square.
options.say: The area will be a perfect square.

quiz.why: Uniform acceleration creates a straight line on the v-t graph, forming a trapezium shape with the time axis.

wrong.0: This would mean zero distance was covered, which is incorrect for acceleration.
wrong.1: Acceleration means the object is moving, so the area must be positive.
wrong.3: The shape depends on the acceleration rate, not necessarily forming a square.
